title: NeuralFLoC: Neural Flow-Based Joint Registration and Clustering of Functional Data
claim: A joint system chains encoding, flow-based alignment, and clustering modules, trained end-to-end through shared losses and feedback.
layout: 4 colored modules, left-to-right, dashed backprop and dotted feedback loops below
description: A wide block diagram split into four rounded colored regions: gray Feature Encoding, blue Neural ODE Warping Engine, blue SRVF Registration, and orange Clustering. Raw functional curves pass through a 1D-CNN encoder trapezoid into a latent space Z_1..Z_n. They then go to an ODE solver, then Boundary Norm and Assignment weight, which produce warping functions and aligned curves. The aligned curves feed an SRVF transform and a registration loss. They also feed a Fourier expansion into spectral coefficients, then cluster centroids with soft assignment and a clustering loss. Both losses combine into a Total Loss box at bottom right. A dashed black Backpropagation arrow runs back to the encoder and ODE solver, and dotted blue Feedback/Guide arrows run to other modules. Small curve plots in blue and orange sit inside the boxes. The eye starts at the raw data on the left and follows the thick black arrows rightward.
caption: Overview of NeuralFLoC. A 1D-CNN encodes raw functional data. A Neural ODE generates smooth, invertible warping functions γi(t) to align curves, and the aligned features are clustered via a Fourier-based soft-assignment module. The model is trained end-to-end for joint registration and clustering.
abstract: Clustering functional data in the presence of phase variation is challenging, as temporal misalignment can obscure intrinsic shape differences and degrade clustering performance. Most existing approaches treat registration and clustering as separate tasks or rely on restrictive parametric assumptions. We present \textbf{NeuralFLoC}, a fully unsupervised, end-to-end deep learning framework for joint functional registration and clustering based on Neural ODE-driven diffeomorphic flows and spectral clustering. The proposed model learns smooth, invertible warping functions and cluster-specific templates simultaneously, effectively disentangling phase and amplitude variation. We establish universal approximation guarantees and asymptotic consistency for the proposed framework. Experiments on functional benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance in both registration and clustering, with robustness to missing data, irregular sampling, and noise, while maintaining scalability. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/NeuralFLoC-FEC8.
